state.row_5_11: 5.11 (pending, Needs 3.12 and 5.9; user decision 8 Nov: persist verified bytes, re-hash on restore, drop a bad scene by name, still start output-inhibited). Done-when: every verified asset the engine accepts, by chunked upload or by path, is written to an engine-owned content-addressed store beside its recovery journal before the publication is acknowledged. On restore each journaled scene's assets are read back from that store and re-hashed before preparation. A scene whose bytes are missing or fail their hash is dropped with a named reason, and the engine still starts output-inhibited; it never refuses to start for it. A real-worker test kills and restarts by each route and takes the restored revision (Taken on T0); a second run with one stored asset removed and another altered starts, names both dropped scenes and their reasons, and still serves the intact scene.
state.planned_design: Store = AssetStore::at_root(<journal file name>.assets) beside the journal (production: %APPDATA%\GrapiX\GrapiX\data\render-engine\recovery.json.assets). The asset plane writes each asset there outside the engine lock, before any acknowledgement; the engine refuses to record bytes its store does not hold (new Refusal::AssetStoreFailed, detail without any filesystem path). Restore reads back and re-hashes every declared asset of every journaled scene, bounded by size; a scene with a missing, altered or unreadable asset is dropped: removed from published, and program/cued cleared only if they name it; the engine still starts at epoch+1, output-inhibited; the journal is then rewritten without the dropped scenes before any port binds. Drops are named on the worker's stderr at start, and Cue/Take/Render of a dropped take is refused with the drop reason itself (an in-memory tombstone, until re-published). Journal schema stays 3, so a 5.9-era journal starts with its asset scenes dropped by name instead of exiting.
verified_facts: gx-engine-host pipes the worker's stderr and reads it only when the child fails to answer, so start-time drop lines are lost on the host route; an undrained pipe could also block a long stderr burst before the port binds.
The journal is rewritten without dropped scenes during attach, before any port binds; in-memory tombstones are forgotten at the next restart.

Today restore is all-or-nothing: if a scene's bytes verify but preparation or GPU preparation fails (a software or capability change, or a transient GPU fault), the worker exits 1 and the journal is left untouched.
AssetStore has no delete; the engine store only grows (files of dropped scenes, altered files, hashes no scene uses).

publish() numbers revisions from the published map only; after a drop removes a take, re-publishing it restarts at Revision(1). Takes pin the content hash, and epoch reconciliation already tolerates a reused revision, but invariants say a version number identifies a publish.

prep_failure_on_good_bytes.instructions: At restore, a scene's bytes verify but preparation or the GPU still refuses it. What should the engine do?

criteria.keep_refusing_to_start: Keep today's refusal to start; the journal stays untouched, so a transient GPU fault cannot erase scenes. The done-when covers only missing or altered bytes.
criteria.drop_by_name_too: Drop that scene by name as well, so no scene can keep the engine down.

store_cleanup.instructions: Should 5.11 remove store files that no journaled scene needs?

criteria.none_follow_up_row: No cleanup in 5.11; file a follow-up row.
criteria.prune_at_start: Prune the store at each start to the restored scenes' hashes, after the journal is rewritten.

drop_report.instructions: How are dropped scenes named durably, given the host discards the worker's stderr on success and the journal no longer lists them after restart?

criteria.report_file_and_stderr: Write every drop, atomically, to a report file beside the journal (<journal file name>.dropped.json) before the journal is rewritten; print a bounded summary on stderr that points to it; the refusal by reason on Cue/Take/Render stays.
criteria.stderr_and_refusal_follow_up: Stderr (capped) plus the refusal by reason only; a follow-up row for a Status/Degradation signal and for the host draining stderr.
criteria.status_field_now: Add a Degradation or EngineStatus field now (contract and TS change).

revision_after_drop.instructions: After a drop, what revision does a re-publish of that take get?

criteria.floor_in_incarnation: The dropped revision plus one, from the in-memory tombstone (no reuse within this run; a later restart may reuse).
criteria.journaled_floor: A revision floor kept in the journal, so a number is never reused (journal schema change).
criteria.allow_reuse: Revision(1) again; the content-hash pin makes reuse safe.

proposal_sound.instructions: Is the planned design sound against the standing rules (verify before use, refusal by name, 3.12's output-inhibited restore and epoch advance, ADR-001's 'a large transfer must never delay a cue')?

needs_user.instructions: Must the user decide any of this before the agent builds it?

breaks_verify_before_use.instructions: Does the planned design use any asset byte that has not been re-hashed against its content address first?

breaks_refusal_by_name.instructions: Does the planned design let any failure pass silently instead of refusing or reporting it by name?

breaks_3_12_output_inhibited.instructions: Does the planned design break 3.12: a forced kill restores without an unrecovered output, the restored engine starts output-inhibited at a new epoch until ConfigureOutput re-arms it?

breaks_adr_001_cue_delay.instructions: Does the planned design let a large asset transfer or write delay a cue or a Program frame (ADR-001)?

breaks_5_9_mutable_path.instructions: Does the planned design break 5.9's rule that the engine never reads a mutable source path later (the user allowed re-reading content-addressed bytes that are re-hashed)?

breaks_published_contract.instructions: Does dropping a published scene at restore break a contract with Playout that a Published revision stays takeable until cleared?

decisions_8_nov_2026.store_cleanup: none in 5.11, follow-up (both models: Laya 0.99, Jev 0.75)
decisions_8_nov_2026.drop_report: user: report file + stderr (Jev report_file 0.78; Laya stderr+follow-up 0.53)
decisions_8_nov_2026.revision_after_drop: user: journaled floor (Laya journaled_floor 0.63; Jev allow_reuse 0.97)
decisions_8_nov_2026.rule_probe: Laya answered 'breaks' at about 0.9 for every rule, contradicting its own 0.88 'sound': no signal. Jev: published contract 0.70, refusal by name 0.66, others 0.21-0.43; both concerns are met by the drop report (user decision) and the refusal by reason.
